findings.title: No safety net left for ungraceful runner death outside systemd
findings.detail: Removing --die-with-parent entirely (rather than, say, keeping it but pinning the spawning thread) means a sandboxed agent process no longer has any kernel-level guarantee of being killed if the runner process itself dies unexpectedly (crash, manual kill -9 during development, non-systemd deployment, etc.). The comment and description correctly note that systemd's KillMode=control-group covers the production path, but anyone running oby-runner outside that unit (local dev, a container without systemd, CI) now has no mechanism at all to stop orphaned bwrap/agent processes — previously overzealous, now absent. Worth calling out explicitly as an accepted trade-off beyond the in-code comment, since orphaned agents still hold worktree/account binds mounted via --bind until something reaps them.
